findings.reason: The original tiles and frozen/current source contain the finite absorbing chain and linear harmonic solution but no figure. A concrete transition graph materially clarifies the two distinct probability roles: outgoing edge weights versus the hitting-probability values at states. N=4 provides a full exact instance without ellipsis or coinciding generic labels; the general N>=1 claim remains unchanged.

diagram_math_checks.evidence: The Statement defines E_N={0,...,N} and p_N(x,y) as transitions from x to y. def-transition-matrix-and-n-step-transition-probabilities defines p(x,y)=K(x,{y}). At N=4 the figure has precisely the five states 0,1,2,3,4, in that order.

Statement and proof step 1.1 give only loops 0->0 and 4->4, each weight 1; the figure contains exactly those loops and no outgoing boundary-to-interior edges. Interior edges are 1->0, 1->2, 2->1, 2->3, 3->2, 3->4, each weight 1/2. Thus each interior row sums to 1 and every displayed edge lies within E_4; no unlisted transition is drawn.
Step 1.2 sets g_N(i)=i/N. The five annotations 0,1/4,1/2,3/4,1 have the required boundary values. Their interior neighbour averages are (0+1/2)/2=1/4, (1/4+3/4)/2=1/2, and (1/2+1)/2=3/4.

def-hitting-return-and-visit-times uses time n>=0, agreeing with the Statement. Step 5.1 identifies g_N(i) with P_i(T_N<T_0); step 6.1 handles endpoints. The caption specializes that existing identity to N=4. The original rigorous proof is byte-preserved and independent of the figure.
